reports.name: Larix decidua
reports.shape: An airy conical selected larch has light-green soft needle clusters on short spurs, single needles on selected longer shoots, pale small twigs, drooping secondary branches and small upright woody seed cones. It is deciduous; a green summer form is displayed.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: Crown remains too open and regularly branched relative to the retained dense summer photograph. Cone and needle dimensions are selected unmeasured proportions; exact spur counts, scale anatomy, cuticle/stomata and seasonal yellowing/abscission are incomplete. Numerical materials remain visibly stylized.

reports.name: Cedrus libani
reports.shape: A selected mature spreading cedar has a forked lower trunk, layered horizontal axes, evergreen short-shoot needle rosettes, single long-shoot needles and upright barrel-shaped woody seed cones with a subdued apex.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: The old-tree crown is still more open and regular than the photographed tree. Fine cone laminae remain smooth and simplified, needle proportions and allometry are unmeasured, and natural bark/needle optics are not calibrated. Cone disintegration and age/population variation are not animated; regional cedar taxonomic boundaries remain source-dependent.

reports.name: Taxus baccata
reports.shape: A detailed selected female leafy shoot has flattened pointed dark-green leaves appearing in two ranks, branching woody axes, an open-tipped red fleshy aril and a separate dark exposed seed. It represents an organ study rather than a complete old yew tree.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: This is a selected female shoot, not a complete mature tree or male reproductive form. Leaves, twig branching and arils remain numerically smooth/regular; stomata, tissue optics, exact dimensions, seed development and old bark are not reconstructed or measured. Partial occlusion is visible in some views.

reports.name: Juniperus communis
reports.shape: A selected multistemmed juniper has irregular strip-bark stems, stiff spreading awl leaves in alternating whorls of three with one pale upper-band cue, and small fused fleshy blue-grey seed cones with a muted wax-bloom appearance.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: The crown remains open and regularly repeated compared with the retained old shrub photograph. Fine band placement, wax bloom, tissue optics and proportions are unmeasured. Prostrate and tree habits, regional/subspecific concepts, cone maturation and seedling development are not represented as universal variation.

reports.name: Cupressus sempervirens
reports.shape: A selected spreading cypress has a forked irregular lower trunk, broad branch groups and nonplanar ultimate shoots clothed in small appressed scale leaves in four ranks; selected compact woody seed cones carry shield-like scale cues.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: Crown outline, branching and bark remain simplified and too regular; leaf scales are coarse at close range and woody shield relief is shallow. Exact scale counts vary in nature; this selected number is not a measured individual. Some foliage overlaps cone landmarks. Natural optics, cultivar/age variation and cone opening are incomplete.

reports.name: Thuja occidentalis
reports.shape: A detailed selected arborvitae shoot branches into flattened fan-like horizontal sprays with small overlapping scale-leaf surfaces and selected small elongated seed cones with thin woody scale cues. This is a leafy organ study rather than a whole mature tree.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: Only a selected shoot is reconstructed. Sprays still have visibly regular saw-toothed edges and gaps; resin glands, fine facial/lateral scale anatomy, wood/cuticle optics and natural proportions are incomplete. The retained photo shows immature green cones whereas the selected reconstruction illustrates a woody mature form; it is not a pixel/colour match to that stage. Cone opening and whole-tree development are unavailable.

reports.name: Metasequoia glyptostroboides
reports.shape: A selected conical dawn redwood has a continuous tapering trunk, opposite-looking paired flat leaves on selected opposite branchlet cues, airy green foliage and small pendent woody seed-cone studies.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: The crown remains tiered, regular and more open than the retained dense mature photograph. Leaf proportions, bark, lower bands, cone grooves and optics are simplified/unmeasured. The reproductive focus is substantially occluded by foliage in the final comparison; its fine morphology cannot be assessed from that view alone. Deciduous shoot loss and complete cone development are unavailable.

reports.name: Araucaria heterophylla
reports.shape: A selected whorled-branch Araucaria habit has horizontal branch groups, incurved narrow foliage cues on selected lower/younger shoots, smaller overlapping adult-like upper foliage and selected large upper-crown globose seed-cone studies.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: Whorls and crown are still too regular/open compared with the mature photograph; transitions in juvenile/adult foliage are simplified and are not an ontogenetic simulation. Cone scale boundaries/prickles, bark, leaf attachment and tissue optics are incomplete/unmeasured. Large selected cones and diagnostic features are not an allometrically fitted individual; Norfolk Island native range is distinct from introduced cultivation.

reports.name: Cycas revoluta
reports.shape: A selected pollen-bearing male cycad has a short rough caudex with old leaf-base cues, a crown of arching pinnate fronds, narrow stiff spine-tipped leaflets with rolled-margin cues and an upright elongated pale pollen-cone study.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: The male form does not represent the different female leafy megasporophyll structure. Old leaf bases remain angular, leaflets too regular, and cone sporophyll details much smoother than the authentic photograph. Revolute margins, stomata, petiole spines, scale/hair microstructure and optics are partial/unmeasured. No fertilization, full development or validated wind mechanics.

reports.name: Zamia furfuracea
reports.shape: A selected low caudex supports radiating pinnate fronds with broad stiff oval leaflets, selected outer-margin tooth cues, subdued longitudinal vein relief and a coarse matte surface. A selected compact reproductive-cone study remains distinct from the fronds.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: Leaflets still appear too smooth, dark and regularly paired; fine farina/hairs, serrations, venation and optical response are incomplete. Caudex/leaf-base and cone surfaces remain artificial at close range; the cone is partly obscured by petioles. The selected cone is not a complete sex/stage series or measured plant, and red-seed exposure/development is not animated.

reports.name: Ephedra distachya
reports.shape: A selected low branching female shrub has connected green internodes, explicit joints, opposite reduced scale-leaf pairs and selected red fleshy paired seed-bract cues with dark exposed seed regions. The stems supply the conspicuous green form.
reports.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
reports.remaining: Stem architecture remains sparse and radially regular compared with the dense authentic shrub. Bracts are smooth and stylized; exact bract fusion, seed exposure, internode dimensions and epidermal detail are unmeasured. Very close support focus clips a foreground stem at the camera near plane. Regional conspecificity is explicitly questioned in the consulted Flora of China; the match does not resolve that taxonomic issue. No seedling development or mechanical/physiological validation.

limits: Partly stylized original educational reconstructions. Fine morphology, age variation, tissue optics, dimensions and environmental mechanics remain incomplete or unmeasured. No independent specialist validation, scientific certification or accuracy percentage. Software checks and screenshots do not establish biological validity.
